parents.title: A Lehmer pair yields an explicit lower bound and an infinite cascade forces nonnegative threshold

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Theorem 1 turns one certified Lehmer-pair statistic into a scalar constraint on the de Bruijn–Newman threshold: a negative environmental term gives a positive-threshold conclusion, while a positive environmental term yields an explicit negative pair-derived lower bound. Corollary 1 then applies a separate limiting step: under an infinite family of positive-environment Lehmer pairs whose gaps shrink to zero, the lower bounds accumulate at zero and force only the one-sided conclusion that the threshold is nonnegative. The scalar compression makes local certificates directly comparable with a global threshold, but the span does not supply the later collision proof or establish that the required infinite family exists; equality at zero remains compatible with the Riemann Hypothesis.

parents.title: Infinitely many shrinking Lehmer gaps force a nonnegative threshold

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The proof normalizes each certified squared gap together with its positive environmental term into a parameter lying in a fixed interval, then expresses the pair-derived threshold bound through a monotone scalar function of that parameter. This removes irrelevant scale and transfers the shrinking-gap limit to the lower-bound limit: under the stated infinite Lehmer-pair hypotheses, the bounds approach zero, and because every one is below the global threshold, they force the one-sided result that the threshold is nonnegative. The argument neither identifies the threshold with zero nor produces the infinite certified family, and its exact normalization is unsafe without the scan.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Extracts the dimensionless limit-transfer mechanism and distinguishes accumulation of lower bounds at zero from equality of the unknown threshold with zero.

parents.title: A much smaller certified gap sharpens the lower bound and motivates an infinite-pair route

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Applying the established pair-to-threshold map to the high-index Lehmer certificate produces the paper’s sharper negative lower bound. Comparing the more precise bound with the leading negative squared-gap term shows that this certificate’s result is only weakly affected by the environmental estimate, which supports a search heuristic favoring exceptionally close pairs that can also be certified. The closing outlook is incremental: further extended zero calculations may supply improved bounds; this span does not prove infinitely many Lehmer pairs, convergence of the bounds to zero, or the Riemann Hypothesis. Exact values and signs remain unsafe without the scan.
